transcript.text: So it's 07:06 and we'll call the planning and zoning meeting to order. And next up on the agenda is roll call and seating of alternates. I see Anne is there. Scott, Steve, Leanne, And myself. Then we got Anne Blanchard is an alternate. It looks like she will not need to be seated at this point. Under additions or changes to the agenda, I did have a couple on the, I'd like to eliminate old business item 5F, the bike path, and item five gs, sale of agricultural products. These will both be covered under new business items and were kind of duplicates.

And then like to add new item six F letter from the Board of Education concerning the community center to new business. And delete item seven approval of the meeting minutes from September 19. Does anybody and I'm. So I make a motion to make those changes. Seconded. Okay, thank you, Steve. Are there any other additions or changes to the agenda? Hearing none, all in favor of the changes as proposed, say aye. Aye. Any opposed? Hearing none, the motion to change the agenda is approved, 500. Next item up is public speak. I see there you want to speak at this point or you want to speak when we get to the new item?

I can give you a preface. Okay, I want to first thank your planning and zoning commission for taking on that letter at a seemingly late time for this meeting. But I want to just first say that nobody wants to see this community center succeed and be built more than I do. I'm in total support of it, and I want to see it fly. And I want to see it fly without interruption. And as a result, Valerie the superintendent of schools came to me with concerns that she had about the process of the construction. And I told her to write it, I asked her to write them down, which she did, and she explained them in a letter that I gave to Jim. Today, and I gave it to Eric Anderson. And we sent to other people in the town, including Adrian, Ed seriously, and Jeff Maguire. And I can't think of anyone else. I would have sent you one Scott, but I knew you would get it through this. Venue here through the planning and zoning. So I want to have these addressed ahead of time, so that nothing gets in the way of the construction cycle of the community center. So that's what I why I gave that letter out. I didn't want it to come at an inopportune moment. I figured we might as well put it out in the open, be honest, and these were the concerns that Valerie had had. So I put them in the letters that I sent out to you, and that's why you received the letter. Hopefully, you'll be able to handle some of the items that are inherent.
It won't be an issue.
Okay. Yeah, and we'll save that discussion for the new business portion of the meeting. But Sure. Certainly, we're all in favor of addressing the items early on. Thank you.
Any other public speak? Hearing none, we'll move into the old business, and the first item is the update on the gravel pit. And agent Halsey, if you can give us an update on that.

Yes, this is in progress. It's going slow, but it is moving forward. I've been in constant contact with Chris Bell, and I've been on-site numerous times. At this time the dirt's moving, the gentleman that's pushing it around does have a plan, copy of the plan. I tried to push it as hard as I can. I realized the time of year is a factor here. I mean they were out there, gentleman was out there today working. I believe there's only one guy. And I will continue to try and reach out to the owner and stay on his back. But other than that,
that's all I got. Are you getting the support? Does it seem like Chris Bell is able to get ahold of the owner?

Chris is yeah he just. He hasn't been able to make him move any quicker either. I hope it's a matter of. Just a few days. I'm looking at the dirt out there and trying to fill and trying to figure out what it's going to take time wise and I don't have a good handle on it. Okay.

My thought is, and I'm going on recollection a little bit at this point, but we approved the Most recent extension to expire on I think it was September 17. With two months to. Restore the site, following the expiration of that. And maybe we should have done that a month earlier if we wanted to get the grass seed planted in a more timely basis and that sort of thing. But I would think that when we get together for our next meeting, as we're putting together the agenda for that, if it's not done to what you think is satisfactory in accordance with the plan, we should ask the owner and Chris Bell to attend and have our lawyer here. I think, you know, I'm almost concerned that we didn't head down the path of getting our attorney here tonight, because you've been getting the runaround on who you're trying to deal with, and you've gone out of your way to get ahold of these guys, and you know, have missed the best weather for getting grass seed planted and that sort of thing. So at that point, I'd be happy to hear any other commission members' thoughts on this particular item.

I would say that we need to tell them that you have a week to get the grass seed done. Completed in the grass seed on. We probably should have done it last time. But that's just my opinion, Jed. It probably could take two hours for that guy to knock that pile down with that loader and the dozer. He hasn't worked in two weeks, Jed, and he knocked down, you know, a fifth of that pile in two hours that he worked this morning because he only works a couple hours, but he hasn't worked in two weeks.

I understand that. Unfortunately, I think we allowed Genovese two months. You know, that our motion. And so I don't know how we can expect, how we can demand anything better than that as long as he's done, you know, within the two month window, which is by the middle of next month. It would certainly be nice to get the grass seed down, and Jim, you can share that with Chris to share with the owner. But I think the point to get across to him is that we're disappointed with the lack of progress. We're disappointed with not being able to get the grass seed down. And if we don't have a better story by next meeting, it is going to be time for us to start legal action.
Look what they did across the street, Jed. I understand completely. You know, is
the example of how, you know, in this labor shortage, things can get done in a hurry.
Every step of the way that gravel operation has not met our expectations. Yep.
We're gonna struggle the whole thing and it was supposed to be done in three or four months when they started. I agree with you Scott.

I would definitely recommend documenting any correspondence we have with them between now and the next meeting so that way we can show a paper trail that, you know, Jim's been pushing this with them and ask for a timeline for completion.

Good ideas. Jim, can you write up a letter to send to them? Know, Certainly. Contact them immediately, tell them what's coming, but we're going to start documenting it because we're not satisfied with the progress that they're making over there? Certainly.

Is the guy you saw moving the dirt around today the same guy that was there when you and I were over there a month ago? Yes, Larry Johnson. Okay, so yeah. He hasn't worked since that day that he was there yet. Has not worked. Okay,

no, agree. I have become totally frustrated with with this particular project, and it would have been so easy to have it go and just be done. And I guess the other question that I had, and I can't remember, Jim, is since it is going so slow, do we have the hay bales, is an erosion control measure, out in place at this point?
Yes. Okay. So I saw the silt fence. Somebody working on the silt fence very recently. I thought it was over the like last Friday, but I could be mistaken about that.

Okay, so Jim, so if you could contact Chris Bell, discuss this with him, follow-up within a week by letter with him, asking him for his schedule. And send, you know, the letter out to the Commission so we know, you know, when it's gone and can stand by to follow-up for the next meeting. Our expectation is that, and you can back me up on my date if I am incorrect there, by November 17, four days prior to our meeting, he is required to be done. And we were very generous in giving him the two month window in his request to do that. I have a couple of questions. Yeah, go ahead, Leanne. Are you finished? I yes.

Your timetable? Just to so basically, Jim, you you used the term pushing dirt around. And did you say that Chris Bell isn't having any more luck compelling this guy to do more work than he has? Are you saying Chris has been in direct contact with him and the guy is not seeing any more responses?

Correct. I mean, he's constantly changed contractors. I think we have the same one that's been in place for a number of months. Yeah, I mean, Chris has been in contact with Bill, Bill Genovese, the owner. And then what happened?

Well, I've tried to have them basically redistribute resources, meaning put somebody full time on there. And that hasn't happened as of yet, but I'll continue to try. I'll deal correctly with Bill I think. Give that a shot. Chris has been very cooperative. It's just. I
don't agree with that statement, Jim. He may have sounded cooperative, but he's not done anything he said he was going to do.
Yeah, I mean the problem is the contractor's not working for Chris.
He works for Genevieve. Yeah. And he only works two hours a day, Chad told me, he's only worked two hours in the last month. Nope, I

gotcha. And I guess the other thing that Jim, you and I should do is we should, you know, set up a meeting here with Mark Branch so that we have our ducks in a row. I'm not real clear on this bonding issue and how that works, but that money is supposed to be put there somewhere and if the owner of the property can't get the restoration plan done, we should tell him that we're going to do it. And if it runs more than the bond that he set aside, he's going to pay for it because he has chosen not to comply with the plan that he agreed to.

So it's the restoration portion that's supposed to have been underway since last month and the ex the excavation, the leveling out or whatever we wanna call it for this know, for tonight, that's what's only been worked on at at the rate of two hours a day intermittently, if that it's not funny. So that's what you're saying has only been done a couple of hours and they're supposed to be into the seeding restoration phase and they haven't even finished the first phase, correct?

Yes, and you know, there's, you see the big mounds over there, there's, you know, piles of tree stumps and tires and that kind of thing over there, and that just needs to get removed and not buried. It's been horrible, just like the initial excavation was. Yes.
So Leanne actually he's worked four hours in the last month maybe five maybe five.
That's That doesn't get any more minimal than that. Exactly. He's not trying at all.
Okay. So we're gonna go with the things that Jed outlined between now and next month as far as the attorney and the bond and directing them that way? Yes. Okay, thank you.

Any other comments on the gravel pit? Okay, I think we covered that. Next, under old business is an update on Rosewood Acres. And I didn't have anything update on that, Jim. I don't know if you did or not.

Well, did contact Grimaldi and he indicated he would be in touch with me to set up a meeting to come in and discuss. He had some personal issues going on that has not done so. I'll follow-up with another phone call, but he's well aware of it. And he's motivated to do this. He just has some other things going on and seemingly hasn't been able to come in.

Are the other members of the commission aware of a Yukon brief this Wednesday at 01:30? Okay, so I see Anne shaking her head, Steve shaking her head. So anyhow, the UConn students are supposed to be helping us out with some economic development kind of stuff. And, you know, I've been trying to, you know, push them towards taking a look at the Rosewood Acres subdivision in light of the fact that Mr. Grimaldi's interested in developing it, maybe they could help with that. I sent out a, you know, I emailed Katherine Lewis, who's kind of the ringleader of of this, you know, asking if she knew whether or not the pitch on Wednesday was going to include anything on Rosewood Acres, and she did not know. If it did, I was going to invite Mr. Brumaldi. I see that the presentation is going to be recorded, and so if there's anything there and it's pretty short notice, Keith Grimaldi will be able to take a look at it on tape, I would hope that the students could work with the town and Mr. Grimaldi to make something happen over there.
Good, can you tell me the particulars of that? Missed that whole.
It's Wednesday at what time and where? At 01:30 in the Community Room. Community Room. And who is doing the presentation?

The UConn students that are working with Andover as their project for the year. Okay, thank you. At the request of Catherine Lewis, it's an economic development kind of project. So, if any of the Commission members or Agent Halsey are available and can attend that, I'm sure that they would appreciate the support of having somebody show up. I plan to go, but I don't know much about what we're going to see.
I'm sorry, you said somebody would be taping that? Do you know? Elaine Buchert is going to it. Elaine's going tape it, okay.

I think it's useful if it's going to be taped. I saw a letter from Adrian that maybe it went to a number of other people too asking Katherine if the presentation could be moved to the evening and I didn't see any response after that. So, if it is still held in the middle of the day, I think it's going to be quite beneficial for people to be able to view it later.

I did see a response on that question, and the response was that a lot of the students have jobs in the evening, and so they weren't available then. And so that's what led I to the didn't cross that letter yet if I got one. Okay. Okay, any other questions or comments on Rosewood Acres, also known as Lindholm Corner? Okay, we're going to move on to 5. Charlie, the update from Planning and Zoning Commission letter to Board of Selectmen regarding speed limit on Route 6. And Leigh Ann drafted up a very nice letter for me. We sent it to the Board of Selectmen. I briefed the Board of Selectmen at last Tuesday's meeting. They were all favorably responsive and agreed to provide a letter to the state reducing the speed limit in that particular area. So I thought that was going well. Then there was, you know, the subject came up, guess Adrian mentioned that I don't know if he saw or the reports of trucks from Route 6 backing into the Dollar General, which was not at all what we were briefed on. And so I think that there have been some questions raised and that sort of thing. So, I think while

everybody remains in agreement that we should lower the speed limit, there might be more to it than that. And I don't know where that stands right now. I know somebody, whether it's Adrian or Eric, has contacted, you know, somebody from the Dollar General and talked to him about that. And it was reported to me that the little design, the design of the parking lot over there, and I didn't think it was radiated area, I thought it was just painted crosshatch on the pavement, but it precluded the ability, the way it was designed to allow a truck that pulled off a Route 6 into the parking lot to make the turn to get around to the loading dock. I personally think that if that's true, you know, they just need to go modify the parking lot so that, you know, to me it's unacceptable To have.
The trucks backing in there from Route 6 and everybody here at the meeting was told that they're going to back in from Link Road. Yep and traffic the traffic consultants

did that report. And yes, Eric did contact Gary, the developer, and discussed the matter. He said that's clearly a driver error and warrants ticket. I mean, it's a traffic offense. And yes, great. The traffic doesn't work, mean, they submitted a plan by their engineer, guaranteeing that this would work. Our engineer reviewed it. I think it's a matter of execution of that turn personally, but nonetheless, I mean, it's gonna be followed up through enforcement.
That whole island that they put in there, Jim, has to be removed. Yeah. There's no way you could, you couldn't even back the landscape trailer around that corner.

I thought you were talking about off of Route 6, the entry. I've got a picture here if I can hopefully pull it up.
Yep, let me see if I can do this. Alright, I think I have to make you a host. Okay, try now, Jed.

Okay, so hopefully you can all see the picture from their site plan for us. And they briefed out the truck would be coming down the road, pull in, go over here, and then back up. And you can see the backup path. Here's the little island that everybody's talking about that raised up a couple of inches. I see. Okay. You can see it. It almost looks like it was planned to back across that in there. Now that, you know, I've gone back to relook at that after we had the problem. And then I interpreted it as based on the brief that they gave us. The truck was coming out and pulls on down the road. I am hoping they don't come back now and say, oh, no. It was always our intention to have the truck back in right like the picture shows. And clearly, that is not what they briefed to us. Luckily, we do have that recorded. But this is the island and,

you know, to expect that the truck is going to back up here and make that sharp turn, it just isn't going to work. And I kind of was, you know, I thought they had traffic engineers and engineers that do trucking turn radiuses and all that kind of stuff, it must have been able to work somehow, now it comes in that it didn't. So anyhow, that's where we're at. The traffic concern is bigger than it was when we were just looking at going down, down the speed limit. The yes? Last

My recollection is that I don't remember any discussion or that anybody would have agreed with them backing in from anywhere. I thought that's why they wanted the curb cut on Route 6 so that trucks could come and go from there. I don't remember any discussion because I brought it up and I think it was because there was kind of an unusual public hearing. Mark Brandt's telling me that it was too late to discuss that. But I had asked at some point could they not come in from Lake Road and pull in front of the building and go around the other end of the building to the loading dock and was told no, there wasn't enough room. So I don't think any of us thought at any point that there was going to be any backing in from anywhere that I thought they were going to come in from the Route 6 curb cut, pull straight in, do what they needed to do with the loading dock and have enough room to come back out Route 6, I guess, because they, you know, they didn't want to talk too much about Lake Road.

No, your recollection is correct. And in fact, you know, I had a question on the permeability of the materials there. Jim cleared that up for me today. Area over here is all permeable material, and I don't think we stand the weight of the trucks coming in there.
Yeah, Jed, I think I even recall, and if we check the video recording, he took his highlighter and drew He did. How they were going to pull in and then back up. Absolutely,

absolutely. There's no doubt in any of our minds what they briefed us to do. Now sometimes, and this is where we need to make sure that we get what we want in writing because, you know, they can brief you one thing and have something different in the plans, and we're going to be held liable to what's in the plans. But in this case, I think the plans show very clearly how they intended to pull the truck in, bag it up here, and we do have that on video. Now the last traffic piece I'll share with the Commission happened today when I was sitting here working on my computer getting ready for the meeting and I saw a car parked out in front of my house for several minutes. I said, I wonder what's up with that. And I stood up, looked over the bushes, and there was a huge Dollar General semi. It looks like it came down Erdoni Road trying to make a right hand turn onto Lake Road. And I think he was struggling and had traffic tied up here for a while. But I don't know what the story was on that, but we were clearly briefed that the delivery trucks were going to come down Route 6 and in here. And the thing that makes me feel the worst about all these traffic issues

is this was probably the number one comment to the public, is concerned about traffic. And if it ends up not being good, I guess, you know, we kind of failed the public with regards to that, although, you know, I thought we had done a very good job of trying to make sure that we understood everything there. But we would certainly be ripe for some criticism if things don't change from what's currently going on. So, but anyhow, that's, that was the result of the lowering of the speed limit discussion. Everybody liked that. I just think there's more to it than that right now and we got to get our hands around that.

So that's what I know about our letter to the Board of Selectmen. It was a good letter, good presentation to the Board of Selectmen. They were all supportive of it, and then it got worse. The next thing on the agenda is lessons learned from the Dollar General application. And so, a couple of weeks back, Eric asked me why we didn't install the sprinkler system in the Dollar General. Because it was required by our subdivision regulations. And I said, well, that was the reason that the applicant came in to subdivide the property first and the site plan second is so that they, you know, one of the reasons could have been, you know, they just wanted to deal with dividing the property first. It could have been that they didn't want to, you know, deal with all the subdivision regulations. I don't know. But again, having done our due diligence, we had the fire marshal and the town engineer at the time take a look at the application, and they both thought it was satisfactory, And in fact, it supports the Connecticut Safety Code. But I went back and talked to Mark Grants about that. He pointed me out to this section in our regulations and I wanted to share that with everybody because it was kind of eye opening to me tonight. I probably should have color coded it here. So when we're looking at compliance with regulations, you know, it says it's going to conform in all respects with these regulations, less variance, blah, blah, blah. Further, the application shall conform to the Andover subdivision regulations. So even though the applicant in this case came in with a site plan,

we can still require and should require compliance with the Andover subdivision regulations, which state that a commercial building will have a sprinkler system in it. You would think that the applicant would have wanted to put a sprinkler system in there for his own protection. But I figured that was his problem. But, you know, the lesson learned for me is we're allowed to enforce our subdivision regulations, even though we're only doing a site plan review. And so I wanted to share that with all you guys. And I think that gives us a little bit of latitude on how to get a better product going forward. So anyhow, I'm not citing you guys at fault, I'm citing myself at fault. And I'm learning. I just wanted to share that opportunity with all you guys.
I should have picked up on that and did not.
I'm still surprised the property owner didn't do it because I would guess his

insurance would be lower with the sprinkler system as well. You know, but I didn't really care. It was his problem, you know, and I thought I was clearly, I had been trained up by a previous town engineer that once the property is subdivided, subdivision regulations don't apply any longer. And so I took it, okay, that's it. Attorney Brandt who says he had his finger in the pie on writing this knew right where to go and pointed it out to me.

There's Steve, you know, apparently Dollar General keeps their stores under the threshold that the National Fire Protection threshold that would kick in the fire sprinkler requirement for that reason. And they're making a financial decision. I understand what you're saying. I agree. It just apparently it doesn't save that much money compared to the cost of this sprinkler

from what I understand. So any other comments on what we learned from the Dollar General? They had a bunch of smart folks in here every meeting they came, and I guess that's why they were paying those folks that money. I was impressed, everybody on the Inland Wetlands Commission was impressed with the magnitude of the driveway construction and how it was going to more than adequately handle the flow that might be going through there. I thought it was a good piece of engineering and in my mind, they did a good job and the finished product looked very nice over there. There. So, moving on, the next item on the agenda is the update of the open space funding for the Ladano property. And we were not able to conclude a successful negotiation on that purchase.

The property owner came back with a counteroffer. We met the counteroffer and still got outbid. And at that point, you know, because we only had so much money in open space funds that we were exceeding the threshold of what the state was allowing to be put in for that, and we couldn't raise our bid anymore. So, thought that would have been a very nice addition for a lot of different ways, but
that one didn't get there. Did we ever find out what the sale price was?

I did not. I figured I could wait and read it in the newspaper when it shows up there. And I think that, you know, probably whoever is buying it is going to come before the Commission at some point wanting to do something with it and we'll be able to get that there. Any other questions on the Ladano property? Okay. Now we're going to move into new business, and the first item up is the annual report. And so, I sent everybody out based on Steve's comment at the last meeting. I put a little paragraph in here about Walda Grant for the multi use path long route 316 wasn't approved. And I'm sure we haven't seen the end of that, but I thought that was a great thing for the town. And I think making safe this ability to navigate that small portion of Route 316 would be important to that project as well and to keep that going. So that's the only thing I added. Steve also pointed out to me, I had a little typo up here. I had R instead of area.

But I know the plan is to put a little picnic table on the other side of the brook there so that people can have a little picnic that are moving along the trail.
Great. No, haven't had time to check it out either. Does anybody know if the picnic table has been put there?
No? Okay, so we'll take that as a lookup. But at this point, I'd like to make a motion for the commission to approve the report as modified here. Second.
Thank you, Steve. And any further discussion on the annual report? Hearing none, I'll call for a vote. Anne? Aye.

Scott? Aye. Steve? Aye. Leigh Ann? Aye. And I vote aye as well. The motion passes five zero zero. I sent everybody out some proposed meeting dates for the coming year.
